analysis: What changed versus the 5:00 AM brief: the last pre-open catalyst landed — October payrolls came in at +165,000, nearly triple the 59,000 forecast, with unemployment ticking down to 4.1%. Futures barely flinched, which is the tell: the market read hot jobs as growth strength already priced in, not a rate shock — but the December hike stays live, and the odds will reprice through the morning. The split tape is unchanged in shape and slightly firmer in the Nasdaq: Nasdaq-100 futures +1.59% (vs +1.50% at 5 AM), S&P +0.26% (vs +0.17%), Dow -0.85% (vs -0.96%), Russell +0.34%. The VIX keeps compressing, 26.88 vs 28.18 at Thursday's close. The earnings dispersion story widened in both directions again: Lam Research joined the paid-in-full list with a $25B buyback (+13% premarket), while DraftKings cratered 24% on a guidance cut and Moderna gave back its beat-and-raise gains, slipping ~2%. Tesla formalized its pivot — Cybertruck production winds down mid-2027 to free Giga Texas for Cybercab — and the stock rose ~2%, the market reading focus rather than failure. The funding-chain question got sharper: the WSJ reports investors now doubt Anthropic can hold a $1.5T IPO valuation, with ~$1T more plausible — a single-source report, but it is the same repricing that drove Thursday's rout. Signal vs noise: the VIX compression, the breadth of the chip bounce (Micron +7.8%, AMD +7.1%, NVDA +4.5%), and the beat-vs-cut earnings split are signal; the thin-volume premarket bounce, Moderna's fade, and the stale Apple order-cut story recirculating are noise until the open and Michigan sentiment at 10 AM ET confirm the tape.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: October payrolls beat big: employers added 165,000 jobs vs the 59,000 forecast, and unemployment ticked down to 4.1%, per BLS figures released at 8:30 a.m. ET. September job growth had been unexpectedly sluggish after months of a low-hire, low-fire environment.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hot print keeps the Fed's December hike live — hike odds were 65-70% before the release — yet futures barely moved, so the market read it as growth strength, not a rate shock.

headlines.headline: The split tape held into 6 AM PT: as of 8:59 a.m. ET, Nasdaq-100 futures were +1.59% at 27,178, S&P 500 futures +0.26% at 7,402, Dow futures -0.85% at 51,176 and Russell 2000 futures +0.34% at 2,745. The VIX fell to 26.88 from Thursday's 28.18 close; the 10-year yield was 4.872%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The Nasdaq-led bounce is intact but still narrow — the Dow falling and the S&P barely green says the rotation out of tech is not done, and the VIX compressing is the one cleanly bullish tell.

headlines.headline: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to make room for increased Cybercab production, Elon Musk said in an X post early Friday. Cybertruck sales have fallen 28% so far in 2026, per Cox Automotive; only 20,237 were sold in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Musk did not say whether production moves elsewhere or ends entirely. Tesla shares rose ~2% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tesla is formally trading a weak-selling truck for its robotaxi bet — Cybercab production began at Giga Texas in April and paid rides started in Austin in September — and the market read it as focus, not failure.

headlines.headline: Nvidia led the Magnificent Seven bounce, +4.53% premarket to $189.83 as of 8:57 a.m. ET. Chip and memory stocks are retracing roughly 30-40% of Thursday's losses, per JPM: Micron +7.8%, AMD +7.1%, Intel +4.7%, Broadcom +4.4%. Lam Research jumped 13.09% after unveiling a $25 billion buyback.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce is broad across semis but still partial — a retracement of a 12.25% SOX rout, not a reversal, until the open holds it.

headlines.headline: Apple remains the only Magnificent Seven name lower premarket, -1.09% to ~$340.42 as of 8:58 a.m. ET, with no fresh company news. Microsoft was -1.01%, Amazon +0.27%, Meta roughly flat and Alphabet -0.1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple is lagging the bounce on no fresh company news — the order-cut story being recirculated is a month old, so the softness reads as relative weakness rather than a new demand signal.

headlines.headline: Anthropic's planned IPO valuation faces scrutiny: some investors are skeptical the AI lab can pull off the $1.5 trillion valuation many earlier expected, and a valuation closer to $1 trillion may be appropriate, according to the Wall Street Journal.
headlines.why_it_matters: The valuation reset is the funding-chain mirror of Thursday's rout — if the marquee AI IPO prices a third lower, the buildout's financing math gets harder. Single-source via the WSJ — treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: Moderna shares slipped ~2% premarket, handing back earlier gains even though Q3 results handily beat expectations — revenue $1.313B vs ~$885M consensus, EPS $0.38 vs an expected $1.25 loss — and the company raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 15-25%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat-and-raise that cannot hold its bounce says buyers are selective even on good prints — profit-taking into strength, not conviction.

headlines.headline: DraftKings gapped down ~24% premarket after slashing guidance to fund a spending push. Lam Research rose 13% on a $25B buyback, and Cloudflare (+19.6%) and Airbnb (+13.7%) held their post-earnings gains as the top premarket gainers.
headlines.why_it_matters: Guidance cuts still get punished hard — the mirror of Cloudflare and Airbnb, where raised outlooks were paid in full. Single-source via one premarket-movers aggregator.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. The $0.525 per-unit distribution pays TODAY, Friday Nov 6, to holders of record Oct 26. The Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. On the call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.
